title: Fixed field of automorphisms is purely inseparable
statement: Let $F$ and $E$ be fields and let $E/F$ be an algebraic normal extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-algebraic-element]. Put $S=\{x\in E: \sigma(x)=x\text{ for every }F\text{-algebra automorphism }\sigma\text{ of }E\}$. Then $S/F$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 030M (lemma-normal-case, line 3666), part (2), with $E_{insep}=E^{\mathrm{Aut}(E/F)}$ as in its proof ('Details omitted'); tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (030M,fields-lemma-normal-case)

proof.text: For an element a of the fixed field, use minpoly.algHom_eq for its injective inclusion into E. Normal.splits' splits its minimal polynomial over E. Every root b is sigma(a) for an F-automorphism sigma, by minpoly.exists_algEquiv_of_root' [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-conjugate-by-automorphism], and so b=a. Conversely minpoly.aeval and minpoly.ne_zero show a is a root. The finite set of distinct roots is exactly {a}.

Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_of_splits identifies the separable degree with the cardinality of this singleton, namely one. Apply isPurelyInseparable_iff_natSepDegree_eq_one to all elements of the fixed field. These are proved Mathlib tools from FieldTheory.SeparableDegree and FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Basic, respectively.
